content.stem: PCN certification is issued by:
options: BINDT, the British Institute of Non-Destructive Testing
distractors: TWI operates the CSWIP scheme, a separate ISO 9712 based scheme.
ASNT operates the American scheme based on SNT-TC-1A and ASNT Central Certification.
The HSE is the regulator for health and safety, not a certification body.
content.explanation: PCN, Personnel Certification in Non-Destructive Testing, is the scheme of BINDT, which acts as the certification body.

content.stem: The PCN scheme is accredited as a certification body against:
distractors: ISO/IEC 17025 applies to testing and calibration laboratories.
ISO 9001 is a general quality management standard and is not sufficient for personnel certification.
ISO 9712 states the technical requirements for NDT personnel; 17024 governs the body that applies them.
content.explanation: ISO/IEC 17024 sets requirements for bodies certifying persons, and accreditation to it is what gives PCN its independence.

content.stem: The technical standard on which PCN certification is based is:
distractors: SNT-TC-1A is the ASNT employer based written practice, a different model.
EN 4179 is the aerospace personnel standard, applied under NANDTB oversight.
ASME Section V is an NDT method standard, not a personnel standard.
content.explanation: PCN is a central certification scheme operating to ISO 9712, which is why PCN certificates are recognised internationally.

content.stem: The essential difference between PCN and an SNT-TC-1A employer based scheme is that:
options: PCN certification is issued by an independent body and is portable between employers
distractors: PCN requires general, specific and practical examinations.
SNT-TC-1A certificates are recertified on a stated cycle and lapse on change of employer.
PCN covers the full range of methods and sectors.
content.explanation: Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies and the certificate normally lapses on leaving. A PCN certificate belongs to the holder.

content.stem: A PCN certificate is issued in respect of a defined:
options: Method, level and sector or product scope
distractors: A method alone would not say what the holder may inspect.
The certificate belongs to the individual, not an employer.
Validity runs five years, not a calendar year.
content.explanation: Every PCN certificate names the method, the level and the industrial sector or product, because competence is sector specific.

content.stem: Typical PCN industrial sectors include:
options: Weld, castings, wrought products and in service inspection
distractors: These are certification levels, not sectors.
These are the examination parts, not sectors.
These are certification prerequisites, not sectors.
content.explanation: Sectors describe the product or application, such as welds or castings, and the specific examination is set against the chosen sector.

content.stem: Under the PCN scheme, the three parts of the qualification examination are:
options: General theory, specific theory and practical
distractors: An oral component is not a standard part of the PCN examination.
No interview is held, and the vision test is a prerequisite rather than an examination part.
Levels are separate certifications, not parts of one examination.
content.explanation: Each method and level is examined by a general theory paper on the method, a specific theory paper on the sector codes, and a practical.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712 and the PCN scheme, the minimum pass mark for each part of the examination is:
distractors: 50 % is well below the required standard.
80 % is above the requirement, although some sector schemes set higher marks for particular sections.
60 % is below the requirement.
content.explanation: A grade of at least 70 % is required in each part separately, so a strong paper cannot carry a weak one.

content.stem: A candidate who passes the general and specific papers but fails the practical:
options: Must retake the failed part within the permitted period and number of attempts
Must retake all three parts immediately
distractors: All parts must be passed for the certificate to be issued.
Passed parts are retained for the stated period.
Re examination is permitted under the scheme rules.
content.explanation: Parts are passed separately, and a failed part may be retaken within the period and attempt limits set by the scheme.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, a candidate who fails a re examination is normally required to:
options: Wait a stated period and undertake further training before applying again
Apply at a lower level automatically
distractors: Exclusion is not permanent.
Re examination is of the whole part, not selected questions.
No automatic downgrade occurs.
content.explanation: The standard sets a waiting period and further training so that repeated attempts are not simply a test of persistence.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, the period of validity of a certificate is:
distractors: Annual renewal applies to the vision test, not the certificate.
Three years is the validity used by some other schemes but not ISO 9712.
Ten years is the recertification interval, which is two full periods.
content.explanation: Certificates run for five years, with renewal at five years and recertification at ten.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, a vision examination must be carried out:
distractors: A single test at certification would not detect deterioration.
Five years is the certificate validity, not the vision interval.
Waiting until recertification would leave gaps of up to ten years.
content.explanation: Near vision and colour differentiation are verified annually and the record is held by the employer.

content.stem: The near vision requirement under ISO 9712 is the ability to read:
options: Jaeger number 1 or Times Roman N4.5 at not less than 30 cm in at least one eye
distractors: Jaeger 5 is a much larger type size and would not demonstrate the required acuity.
Snellen charts measure distance vision, which is not the near vision requirement.
Colour differentiation is a separate additional requirement.
content.explanation: Near vision is tested with Jaeger 1 or equivalent at 30 cm or more, with or without correction, in at least one eye.

content.stem: The colour vision requirement under ISO 9712 is that the candidate:
options: Can distinguish and differentiate the contrast between the colours used in the method
Is free of any colour deficiency
Can name all colours in the spectrum
distractors: Perfect colour vision is not required.
A deficiency that does not affect the colours used in the method is not disqualifying.
Naming colours is not the test.
content.explanation: The requirement is functional: the candidate must be able to distinguish the colours relevant to the method being used.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, renewal of certification at the end of the five year period normally requires:
options: Evidence of continued satisfactory work activity and a current vision test
A full re examination in every case
distractors: Full re examination belongs to recertification at ten years, and even then there are defined routes.
Payment alone does not evidence continued competence.
Fresh training is required only where the activity condition is not met.
content.explanation: Renewal is a documentary process based on continued activity without significant interruption, plus the annual vision record.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, recertification after ten years normally requires:
options: A practical examination or, where permitted, a structured credit assessment
Nothing, if renewal was granted at five years
distractors: Renewal at five years does not discharge the ten year obligation.
A theory paper alone does not demonstrate practical competence.
Training attendance is not by itself evidence of competence.
content.explanation: At ten years the holder demonstrates continued competence, most commonly by practical examination, with a structured credit route available in some schemes.

content.stem: Significant interruption under ISO 9712 means:
options: An absence from the method that prevents the holder from claiming continued activity
Any holiday of more than two weeks
distractors: Normal leave is not a significant interruption.
Changing employer does not by itself interrupt the activity, since PCN certificates are portable.
A sector change may require a further specific examination but is not itself an interruption.
content.explanation: A significant interruption is a period away from the method long enough to call continued competence into question, and it affects renewal.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, a certificate may be suspended or withdrawn where the holder:
options: Fails to meet the conditions of certification, including ethical conduct
Works in more than one sector
distractors: Portability is a feature of the scheme, not a breach.
Leave does not affect certification.
Multiple sector scopes are normal where each has been examined.
content.explanation: The certification body may suspend or withdraw for breach of conditions, including falsification of records or unethical conduct.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, the body that conducts the examination on behalf of the certification body is:
options: The candidate's employer in all cases
distractors: Employer conducted examination is the SNT-TC-1A model, not ISO 9712.
Regulators do not conduct NDT examinations.
A training provider must be separately authorised as an examination centre.
content.explanation: Examinations are conducted at authorised qualification bodies, examination centres operating under the certification body's control.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712 the training body and the examination must be separated so that:
options: The examination remains independent of the training provided
The employer can set the questions
distractors: Fees are a consequence, not the purpose.
Minimum training durations are set by the standard and are not shortened.
Employers do not set examination questions under a central scheme.
content.explanation: Independence between instruction and examination is what makes a central certification scheme credible.

content.stem: A PCN Level 1 holder is authorised to:
options: Carry out testing to written instructions under Level 2 or Level 3 supervision
Interpret and evaluate results against codes independently
Select the test method for a job
distractors: Procedure approval belongs to Level 3.
Independent evaluation against codes belongs to Level 2.
Method selection belongs to Level 3.
content.explanation: Level 1 performs the test to instructions and reports the raw result. Interpretation against acceptance criteria is a Level 2 function.

content.stem: A PCN Level 2 holder is authorised to:
options: Set up and calibrate equipment, interpret and evaluate results against codes, and write NDT instructions
Approve NDT procedures and qualify personnel
distractors: Procedure approval and personnel qualification are Level 3 functions.
Working under supervision describes Level 1.
Certification is the function of BINDT, not an individual.
content.explanation: Level 2 carries the working responsibility: setting up, evaluating against acceptance criteria, writing instructions and reporting.

content.stem: A PCN Level 3 holder is authorised to:
options: Establish and approve procedures, select methods and techniques, and assist in qualifying personnel
distractors: Supervision is one part of a much wider responsibility.
Level 3 may perform testing but that is not the distinguishing authority.
Certificates are issued by BINDT as the certification body.
content.explanation: Level 3 carries full technical responsibility for the NDT programme, including procedure approval and method selection.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, responsibility for verifying that a candidate's stated industrial experience is genuine rests with:
options: The employer, who attests it, subject to verification by the certification body
distractors: A self declaration without employer attestation is not accepted.
Training providers evidence training, not industrial experience.
The examiner assesses the examination, not the experience record.
content.explanation: Experience is attested by the employer in a documented form and is subject to verification by the certification body.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, experience gained in more than one method may be credited:
options: Pro rata, with the total not less than the sum required and each method meeting its own minimum share
In full for every method simultaneously
Only if gained with one employer
distractors: Counting the same time in full for several methods would overstate experience.
Experience in secondary methods can be credited when properly documented.
Experience with several employers is acceptable if attested.
content.explanation: Where a candidate works across methods, experience is apportioned, and the standard sets how the total and the per method minimum are calculated.

content.stem: Under the PCN scheme, an appeal against an examination result is made:
options: To BINDT under the published appeals procedure, within the stated time limit
To the Health and Safety Executive
distractors: An informal approach to the examiner is not the defined route.
The employer has no authority over the certification body's decisions.
The HSE regulates health and safety, not certification.
content.explanation: The scheme publishes an appeals and complaints procedure with defined routes and time limits, which is a requirement of ISO/IEC 17024.

content.stem: Under the PCN scheme, candidates are required to sign a code of ethics because:
options: Certification depends on honest reporting and conduct as well as technical skill
distractors: Ethics undertakings do not replace any examination.
Experience requirements are unaffected.
ISO 5817 is a weld quality standard, unrelated to personnel conduct.
content.explanation: The scheme conditions include a code of ethics, and breach of it is grounds for suspension or withdrawal.

content.stem: Falsifying an NDT report is treated under the PCN scheme as:
options: Grounds for withdrawal of certification, independent of any legal consequence
A matter for the employer only
Acceptable if no defect was missed
distractors: The certification body acts on its own account in addition to any employer action.
Falsification is not administrative.
The absence of consequence does not make a false record acceptable.
content.explanation: The certification body may withdraw certification for such conduct, and the fact that no harm resulted is not a defence.

content.stem: An NDT instruction, as distinct from an NDT procedure, is:
options: A written description of the steps for a specific application, derived from an approved procedure
A more authoritative document than a procedure
A record of the results obtained
distractors: The procedure is the senior document.
Results are recorded in the report.
National standards sit above both.
content.explanation: The procedure states how the method is applied generally and is approved by Level 3. The instruction applies it to a particular job and may be written by Level 2.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712 the employer, as distinct from the certification body, remains responsible for:
options: Authorising the certified individual to operate on the employer's equipment and products
distractors: Examination content is controlled by the certification body.
Certificates are issued by BINDT.
Pass marks are set by the standard and the scheme.
content.explanation: Certification proves generic competence. The employer still issues a written authorisation covering its own equipment, procedures and products.
